title: Closed and open-source models: licence, cost and control

videos.script: Closed or open is the first fork in choosing a model, and the words hide more than they say. {{kinds}} Sort models by what you are given. An endpoint. The weights, under conditions. Or the weights with no conditions at all. {{licences}} Then read the conditions. A ceiling on how many users you may have. A ban on training other models with the outputs. A name you have to display when you ship it. {{code}} And a trap: the licence on the repository is often the licence for the code, not for the weights. {{cost}} Then the price. One open model, ten hosts, and almost seven times between the cheapest and the dearest. One closed model, seventeen routes, and nearly one price. {{retire}} Then time. A closed model is retired on a date the provider sets. A file of weights on your disk answers the same way in ten years. {{data}} Last, the e-mail itself, and where it goes.
